strings.museum.name: Museum of Far East Remembrance
strings.hero.title: Modern China and the wider world, through original objects.
strings.hero.lede: Based in Canada, MOFER collects, digitizes, studies, and shares the history of the Far East through exhibitions and education.
strings.page.collections.title: Collections
strings.page.collections.lede: Original objects from late Qing China, wartime Asia and Chinese lives overseas.
strings.page.exhibitions.title: Exhibitions
strings.page.exhibitions.lede: Two exhibitions at Boynton House connect China's wartime experience, international alliances and postwar justice through original documents, photographs and objects.
strings.intro.label: History in the originals
strings.intro.title: Photographs, letters and posters connect late Qing and Republican China, the Second World War in Asia, and postwar justice. Other holdings trace Chinese lives and culture across the Pacific.
strings.facts.objects: More than 100 original documents, photographs, and objects shown in our first exhibition in 2025.
strings.facts.base: A Canadian base for cross-cultural research and education
strings.about.label: About MOFER
strings.about.title: A Canadian museum initiative, bringing modern Chinese and Far East history into public view.
strings.about.bodyOne: MOFER is an independent museum initiative in Canada. We collect and preserve original archives and cultural objects from China and the modern Far East.
strings.about.bodyTwo: The objects shown here follow China's changing place in the world, from late Qing diplomacy and the 1911 Revolution to wartime alliances and the postwar trials. Chinese Canadian and Chinese American material connects these histories to life overseas.
strings.about.bodyThree: Our holdings include original photographs, documents, books, periodicals, posters, maps, and unpublished manuscripts. We present them through travelling exhibitions and institutional partnerships.
strings.collections.label: Collection highlights
strings.collections.title: Three objects, three ways into the past.
strings.collections.intro: Eight objects. Choose a theme, or enlarge an original to look closely.
strings.pathways.label: More to explore
strings.pathways.title: Follow a thread through the archive.
strings.pathways.intro: These six themes connect individual objects to histories of war, relief, political change and everyday life.
strings.pathways.children.title: Children and wartime relief
strings.pathways.children.body: Photographs of children and orphans, relief publications, and overseas fundraising records trace aid to the youngest victims of war.
strings.pathways.sutton.title: The Sutton files
strings.pathways.sutton.body: Letters about the Tokyo Trial, the University of Nanking, and postwar investigations offer a way to study justice, testimony, memory, and evidence.
strings.pathways.medical.title: Medicine, humanitarian aid, and care
strings.pathways.medical.body: Medical instruments, nursing texts, and relief records document treatment, transport, and support beyond the battlefield.
strings.pathways.publications.title: Children's publications
strings.pathways.publications.body: Educational and public-facing publications for children across the Pacific brought the Far East into North American classrooms and homes.
strings.pathways.qing.title: Late Qing China in photographs
strings.pathways.qing.body: Photographs from the late nineteenth and early twentieth centuries record China amid war, treaties, and international photography.
strings.pathways.portrait.title: Portraits and identity
strings.pathways.portrait.body: Portraits, inscriptions, and original mounts offer clues to personal identity, social status, and visual culture.
strings.exhibition.label: Past exhibition
strings.exhibition.summary: Our first independently curated exhibition ran at Boynton House in Richmond Hill, Ontario, Canada, from September 9 to 14, 2025, marking 80 years since the end of the Second World War.
strings.exhibition.featureTitle: The Far East's place in Allied victory.
strings.exhibition.featureBody: More than 100 original photographs, documents, books, periodicals, and objects were shown, many for the first time in North America. Three sections shaped the exhibition: International Support and Cooperation, China Fights Back, and Victory.
strings.gallery.uniform: Uniforms, posters, and historical photographs on display.
strings.gallery.archive: Original documents and photographs, on public view.
strings.gallery.guided: Guided tours and public education for visitors of different ages and backgrounds.
strings.gallery.poster: Wartime posters help tell the story of a forgotten ally.
strings.research.label: Research & education
strings.research.title: Opening the collection to research and learning.
strings.work.collect.title: Collecting & preservation
strings.work.collect.body: We record where each item came from, its condition, and its materials to support research and digitization.
strings.work.digitize.title: Digitization & cataloging
strings.work.digitize.body: We digitize photographs, documents, manuscripts, books, and objects so their records can be searched and cited.
strings.work.research.title: Research & collaboration
strings.work.research.body: We work with museums, archives, universities, researchers, and educators to study Far East history in a global context.
strings.work.education.title: Exhibitions & education
strings.work.education.body: Pop-up exhibitions, classroom materials, lectures, and community programs make history open to discussion.
strings.contact.label: Collaborate with MOFER
strings.contact.title: For exhibition proposals, collection questions and collaboration.
strings.contact.body: Museums, archives, universities, researchers, educators, community groups, and volunteers are welcome. Write to us about exhibitions, research, translation, public programs, or archival preservation.

collections.title: Tim Louie's Victory Address in Vancouver's Chinatown
collections.summary: At the end of the Second World War, Vancouver community leader Tim Louie honoured Chinese Canadians' contributions at the front and at home.
collections.context: Chinese Canadians and the end of the Second World War, 1945.
collections.look: Look at the signs and the people gathered around the speaker. What connects this public celebration in Vancouver to a war fought across the Pacific?

collections.title: China's Army is a Seasoned Military Team
collections.summary: Milton Caniff's large poster introduced American audiences to China's armed forces and their cooperation with the Allies in the war against fascism.
collections.context: China and the Allied coalition during the Second World War.
collections.look: Compare the uniforms and figures in the main scene with the smaller illustrations below. How does the poster present cooperation between allies?

collections.title: Produce for Victory!
collections.summary: Made after Pearl Harbor, this poster used Chinese soldiers to call for planes, tanks, and guns for an Allied victory.
collections.context: American wartime production and support for China's resistance to Japan.
collections.look: Read the headline, then look at the soldiers' faces. How do a few words and a portrait turn military production into a personal appeal?

collections.title: Draft Testimony of Witness Zhou Yiyu
collections.summary: Zhou Yiyu, Chongshantang's general manager, testified that the charity buried more than 110,000 bodies after the Nanjing Massacre. His testimony became evidence in the postwar trials.
collections.context: The Nanjing Massacre and the use of testimony in postwar trials.
collections.look: Notice the handwritten columns and the physical page. What can an original draft tell us that a later printed account cannot?

collections.title: Letter from Pearl S. Buck
collections.summary: Nobel laureate Pearl S. Buck wrote as chair of the China Emergency Relief Committee to thank a donor for supporting China's war effort and humanitarian relief.
collections.context: International humanitarian relief during China's war against Japan.
collections.look: Look for the committee's heading, the date and the signature. How does one donor's letter connect a person in New York to relief in China?

collections.title: Xinhai Revolution Photographs Collection
collections.summary: MOFER holds more than 30 original photographs of the Xinhai Revolution, including events in Wuhan, Nanjing, Shanghai, Xi'an, and Canton.
collections.context: The 1911 Revolution and China's transition from imperial rule.
collections.look: Compare the people, clothing and setting in this photograph. Which details could you use to ask further questions about political change?

collections.title: Signing of the Boxer Protocol
collections.summary: An original photograph of the Boxer Protocol signing, where Prince Qing and Li Hongzhang represented the Qing government.
collections.context: Late Qing diplomacy following the Boxer conflict, 1901.
collections.look: Look at where the participants sit and stand. How does the arrangement of a signing ceremony represent political authority?

collections.title: Anna May Wong Collection
collections.summary: Anna May Wong was the first Chinese American film star to gain international recognition. The collection includes original photographs, multilingual magazines, tobacco cards, autographs, commemorative coins, and film posters.
collections.context: Chinese American cinema and international cultural life in the twentieth century.
collections.look: Look at the people surrounding Anna May Wong. How might a photograph record both a film star's public image and her encounters across cultures?
